description: Kuwait Ministry of Health mandatory health insurance coverage requirements under Kuwait's Health Insurance Law No. 1 of 1999 and subsequent MOH Ministerial Resolutions. All licensed health insurance providers operating within the State of Kuwait must comply with minimum benefit levels, copayment caps, and coverage mandates as stipulated by the Ministry of Health. These directives apply to all employer-sponsored and individual health insurance policies issued or renewed on or after the effective date.

clauses.title: Mandatory Inpatient Coverage
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies issued in the State of Kuwait shall provide inpatient hospitalization coverage at a minimum standard of general ward accommodation in MOH-licensed facilities. The insurer shall cover room and board, nursing care, physician fees, diagnostic services, surgical procedures, anesthesia, medications administered during the hospital stay, and post-operative care. Where a policyholder elects accommodation above the general ward standard, the insurer shall cover costs equivalent to the general ward rate and the policyholder shall bear the differential. Copayment for inpatient admissions shall not exceed KWD 10 per admission episode, and the total annual copayment obligation for inpatient services shall not exceed KWD 300 per insured person per policy year.
clauses.regulatory_note: Per MOH Ministerial Resolution No. 320/2019, all insurers must guarantee general ward inpatient coverage. Failure to provide minimum inpatient benefits is subject to penalties under Article 14 of the Health Insurance Law.

clauses.title: Mandatory Outpatient Coverage
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies shall include outpatient medical services coverage encompassing general practitioner consultations, specialist consultations upon referral, diagnostic laboratory tests, radiological imaging, and prescribed outpatient medications. The insurer may apply a coinsurance rate not exceeding 20% of the approved outpatient service charge, provided that the insured person's copayment per outpatient visit shall not exceed KWD 5 regardless of services rendered during that visit. Outpatient coverage shall extend to all MOH-approved clinics, polyclinics, and hospital outpatient departments within the State of Kuwait.
clauses.regulatory_note: MOH Directive 2019/047 mandates that outpatient coinsurance shall not create a financial barrier to accessing primary and secondary care. The KWD 5 per-visit cap applies irrespective of the coinsurance percentage calculation.

clauses.title: Mandatory Emergency Treatment
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies shall provide full coverage for emergency medical treatment at any licensed healthcare facility within the State of Kuwait, whether or not the facility is within the insurer's approved network. Emergency treatment is defined as medical care required for a condition that, if not immediately treated, could reasonably be expected to result in serious impairment to bodily functions, serious dysfunction of an organ or body part, or death. No copayment, coinsurance, deductible, or prior authorization shall be imposed on emergency treatment claims. The insured or the treating facility shall notify the insurer within 24 hours of the emergency admission or visit. Failure to provide timely notification shall not constitute grounds for claim denial where the emergency nature of the condition is medically substantiated.
clauses.regulatory_note: Under Article 8 of the Health Insurance Law and MOH Circular No. 112/2020, insurers are strictly prohibited from denying, reducing, or delaying emergency claims on the basis of network restrictions, prior authorization requirements, or notification delays.

clauses.title: Mandatory Maternity Benefits
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies covering female insured persons shall include maternity benefits comprising antenatal care, delivery, and postnatal care. The maximum waiting period for maternity benefits shall not exceed 12 months from the policy effective date or the date of continuous coverage commencement. Antenatal coverage shall include a minimum of 6 antenatal consultation visits with an obstetrician or qualified midwife, routine antenatal laboratory tests, and ultrasound scans as medically indicated. Delivery coverage shall provide a minimum benefit of KWD 2,000 for normal vaginal delivery and KWD 3,500 for caesarean section delivery, inclusive of hospital stay, physician fees, anesthesia, and related services. Newborn coverage shall be automatically extended from the date of birth for a period of 30 days under the mother's policy at no additional premium, covering routine neonatal care, vaccinations, and medically necessary treatment.
clauses.regulatory_note: MOH Resolution No. 215/2019 on Maternity and Reproductive Health Coverage requires all insurers to provide maternity benefits as a core component of compliant health insurance policies. The 30-day automatic newborn extension is mandated by MOH Directive 2020/003.

clauses.title: Mandatory Pharmacy Coverage
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies shall cover prescription medications listed in the Kuwait National Formulary as approved by the Ministry of Health. For outpatient prescriptions, the insurer may apply a copayment of no more than 25% of the medication cost for brand-name drugs and no more than 10% for generic equivalents where a generic alternative is available and prescribed. For medications dispensed during an inpatient admission, no copayment or coinsurance shall be charged to the insured person. The insurer shall maintain an approved drug formulary that includes, at a minimum, all medications listed in the MOH Essential Medicines List.
clauses.regulatory_note: MOH Pharmaceutical Affairs Directive No. 88/2020 governs minimum pharmacy coverage standards. Insurers must update their formularies within 60 days of any revision to the Kuwait National Formulary or MOH Essential Medicines List.

clauses.title: Maximum Copayment Caps
clauses.full_text: The Ministry of Health establishes the following maximum copayment and coinsurance limits to ensure that cost-sharing arrangements do not create undue financial burden on insured persons. For outpatient services, the maximum coinsurance rate is 20% of the approved charge, subject to a cap of KWD 5 per visit. For emergency services, no copayment or coinsurance shall be applied. For inpatient admissions, the maximum copayment is KWD 10 per admission episode. The total annual out-of-pocket expenditure by any insured person for copayments and coinsurance combined shall not exceed KWD 2,000 per policy year. Once the annual out-of-pocket maximum is reached, the insurer shall cover 100% of all eligible charges for the remainder of the policy year. These caps apply to all plan types and may not be waived or increased by contractual arrangement between the insurer and the policyholder.
clauses.regulatory_note: MOH Resolution No. 320/2019 Annex B establishes binding copayment caps. Insurers found to exceed these limits are subject to fines under Article 16 of the Health Insurance Law and potential license suspension under MOH enforcement procedures.

clauses.title: Minimum Annual Benefit Limit
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies issued in the State of Kuwait shall provide a minimum annual benefit limit of not less than KWD 30,000 per insured person per policy year. This aggregate annual limit shall encompass all covered inpatient, outpatient, emergency, pharmacy, and ancillary services. Emergency treatment shall carry a standalone minimum sub-limit of KWD 30,000 per policy year, which shall not be exhausted by non-emergency utilization. Maternity benefits shall carry minimum sub-limits of KWD 2,000 for normal vaginal delivery and KWD 3,500 for caesarean section delivery. Insurers may offer policies with higher benefit limits but shall not issue, renew, or amend any policy to provide aggregate annual benefits below the prescribed minimums.
clauses.regulatory_note: The KWD 30,000 minimum annual benefit limit is established under MOH Directive 2020/001. Policies with benefit limits below this threshold shall not receive MOH certification and are considered non-compliant under Article 5 of the Health Insurance Law No. 1 of 1999.

clauses.title: Prohibited Exclusions — Conditions Insurers May Not Exclude
clauses.full_text: Health insurance policies issued in the State of Kuwait shall not exclude or restrict coverage for the following conditions and services, which the Ministry of Health deems essential to public health objectives: (a) HIV/AIDS testing, counseling, and treatment, including antiretroviral therapy and related monitoring, shall be covered as any other chronic condition without discrimination or additional cost-sharing; (b) Mental health and psychiatric services shall be covered for a minimum of 10 inpatient days per policy year and reasonable outpatient psychiatric and psychological consultations; (c) Dialysis services, including hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis for insured persons with end-stage renal disease or acute kidney injury, shall be fully covered without annual session limits; (d) Cancer screening and early detection services, including mammography, cervical screening, colorectal screening, and prostate screening as per MOH Cancer Screening Guidelines, shall be covered at 100% with no copayment for preventive screening performed at recommended intervals.
clauses.regulatory_note: MOH Circular No. 75/2020 on Prohibited Exclusions mandates that insurers may not deny, exclude, or limit coverage for the listed conditions. Violations are subject to enforcement action under Article 17 of the Health Insurance Law, including mandatory policy amendment, fines, and reporting to the Insurance Regulatory Unit.

clauses.title: Maximum Waiting Period Caps
clauses.full_text: The Ministry of Health prescribes the following maximum waiting periods applicable to health insurance policies issued in the State of Kuwait. For pre-existing diseases and conditions declared at the time of policy inception, the maximum waiting period shall not exceed 6 months from the policy effective date, after which full coverage must be extended for the declared condition subject to all other policy terms. No waiting period shall be imposed for emergency medical treatment regardless of the nature of the underlying condition, including emergencies arising from pre-existing diseases. No waiting period shall be imposed for complications of pregnancy, including ectopic pregnancy, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, gestational diabetes requiring hospitalization, and emergency caesarean section, provided the insured person has active coverage at the time the complication occurs. Standard maternity benefits remain subject to the 12-month maximum waiting period as prescribed under Section MOH-KW-2.4.
clauses.regulatory_note: MOH Directive 2020/005 on Waiting Period Standardization prohibits insurers from imposing waiting periods exceeding the prescribed maximums. The continuity of coverage provision under Article 9 of the Health Insurance Law ensures that insured persons do not face repeated waiting periods when renewing or transferring policies without a significant coverage gap.
